jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) – Institute for Pharmacology and ToxicologyRef.-Nr.  601-2026Third-party fundingThe Faculty of Medicine is an integral part of the Otto-von-Guericke-University Magdeburg and cooperates with the Magdeburg University Hospital A.ö.R. in research, teaching and patient care.Your Responsibilities:We are seeking two highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellows to join our team investigating the molecular and cellular organization of the nervous system using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics approaches. The successful candidates will work at the interface of neuroscience, genomics, and computational biology to map gene expression patterns across brain tissue with spatial resolution, contributing to our understanding of neural circuit organization, development, and disease.This is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative, well-resourced research environment with access to state-of-the-art spatial profiling platforms (e.g., MERFISH, 10x Visium), advanced microscopy, and high-performance computing infrastructure.Two positions are available with complementary focus:- Position 1 — Experimental/Wet-lab focus: Designing and executing spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue, including tissue preparation, probe design, imaging, and data generation- Position 2 — Computational/Analytical focus: Developing and applying computational pipelines for spatial transcriptomic data analysis, including cell-type mapping, spatial statistics, and integration with single-cell/single-nucleus datasets(Candidates with strong interest and skills spanning both areas are also encouraged to apply and may be considered for either position.)Key Responsibilities:- Design, plan, and conduct spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue samples- Analyze and interpret complex spatial and single-cell genomic datasets- Collaborate with neuroscientists, computational biologists, and clinicians within and outside the group- Present findings at lab meetings, seminars, and international conferences- Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication- Contribute to grant writing and mentoring of graduate/undergraduate students- Maintain rigorous documentation and adhere to good research and data management practicesYour Profile:Essential Qualifications:- A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Neuroscience, Molecular/Cell Biology, Genomics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related field- Demonstrated research productivity (peer-reviewed publications and/or preprints)- Strong written and verbal communication skills in EnglishFor the experimental-focus position, in addition:- Hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques (e.g., histology, immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, RNA-seq library prep)- Experience with spatial transcriptomics platforms (e.g., Visium, MERFISH, Xenium, seqFISH) is highly desirable- Experience with rodent or human brain tissue handling is a plusFor the computational-focus position, in addition:- Strong programming skills (Python and/or R)- Experience analyzing single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data- Familiarity with relevant packages/tools (e.g., Scanpy, Seurat, Squidpy, STUtility) and statistical/machine learning methods- Experience with high-performance/cluster computing is a plusWe offer:- Access to cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and imaging technology- A collaborative, interdisciplinary, and supportive research environment- Funding and support to attend international conferences- Opportunities for career development, mentoring, and grant-writing training- Work and family in harmony: Through Klinikzwerge (https://kita.med.ovgu.de/) , childcare may be available, subject to availability- Help protect the environment and enjoy discounted public transportation through a job ticket- In addition, we offer a diverse range of sports and relaxation activities as part of our workplace health promotion program- Onboarding: At the start of your employment, you will participate in our orientation program, where you will receive important information and training sessionsTerms and Conditions:- **Salary: **The salary group E 13 according to “Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder” awaits you- **Appointment: **The position is to be filled as a full-time position, with a workload of 2,5 years, starting on 2027/01/01- Work Location: Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg, Medizinische Fakultät, Leipziger Str. 44, 39120 Magdeburg- **Application Deadline: **2026/10/31For further questions, please contact Mrs. Dr. Julia Rödiger at julia.roediger@med.ovgu.deYour application:Please submit the following as a single PDF:1. A cover letter describing your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation for applying (max 1–2 pages)2. A full CV, including a list of publications3. Contact details for two–three references[online application](https://onlinebewerbungsserver.de/ApplyForm/AppStart.aspx?c=U_CD_11_3E_FB_F1_D5_60_F8_C3_189_FD_1C_D3_A9_C8_B3_A6_F9_09_FB_E3_03S_86_C4_8B_A5_B4_AF_1F_BFc_13_DE_F1_99_D3_A6_D1_9D_A4_1Dc_E5C_3A)by E-Mail:E-Mail schreiben (LzI3MKWvqJ5aDT1yMP5iqzq1YzEy)  - (Reference number: 601-2026)by Post:Otto von Guericke University MagdeburgFaculty of MedicinePersonnel Division - RecruitingReference number: 601-2026Leipziger Str. 44, 39120 MagdeburgIf you have an international vocational or academic qualification, your application must be accompanied by a certificate evaluation (https://www.med.ovgu.de/Forschung/Klinische+Studien/Patient+and+Public+Involvement/PPI_Glossar/Evaluation.html) from the Central Office for Foreign Education (KMK) (https://www.kmk.org/zab/zentralstelle-fuer-auslaendisches-bildungswesen/allgemeines-zur-anerkennung.html) . TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. Founded in 1828, today it is a globally oriented, regionally anchored top university as it focuses on the grand challenges of the 21st century. It develops innovative solutions for the world's most pressing issues. In research and academic programs, the university unites the natural and engineering sciences with the humanities, social sciences and medicine. This wide range of disciplines is a special feature, facilitating interdisciplinarity and transfer of science to society. As a modern employer, it offers attractive working conditions to all employees in teaching, research, technology and administration. The goal is to promote and develop their individual abilities while empowering everyone to reach their full potential. TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Institute of Communication Technology, the Deutsche Telekom Chair of Communication Networks offers a project position within the EFRE-project Robots4ResQ asResearch Associate (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited until December 31, 2027. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz – WissZeitVG).Tasks: - design and implement advanced control, state estimation, and path planning algorithms for single and multi-agent robotic systems (UAVs)- develop and train AI models for practical applications such as real-time object detection and tracking in complex environments- create and manage high-fidelity simulation environments for autonomous systems using tools like Gazebo, Nvidia Isaac, and ROS2- research and evaluate robust communication protocols (e.g., MAVLink) for swarm systems to ensure reliable data exchange and cooperative control- lead the development of practical demonstrators, from embedded flight controller design to system integration- publish research findings in high-impact international journals and conferences, contributing to the academic communityRequirements: - university degree (Master's or equivalent) in Mechatronics, Electrical-Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field- proven hands-on experience in software development with Modern C++ and Python - demonstrable expertise in robotics software, particularly ROS, and simulation platforms like Gazebo- a strong foundation in control systems design, simulation, and implementation, preferably shown through projects with UAVs or other robotic systems- practical experience implementing AI models for tasks such as object tracking or SLAM- full professional proficiency in English (spoken and written)- elementary knowledge of German is welcomed- an independent, proactive, and scientific-work-oriented mindset with the ability to thrive in a team environmentWe offer: - the opportunity for engaging and independent work within a flat hierarchy, in an open-minded team and supportive atmosphere- flexible arrangements for work hours to support a good work-life balance- 30 days of vacation per year (based on a 5-day workweek)- extensive opportunities for professional development and continuing education- health care and sports programs offered by TUD- a discounted job ticket (also available as a Deutschlandticket)- participation in the supplementary pension scheme for employees in the public sector via VBL (Federal and State Government Employees Retirement Fund)TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.Application:Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents by October 28, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de/) by sending it as a single pdf file to karin.domel@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:karin.domel@tu-dresden.de)  or to:TU Dresden, Deutsche Telekom Professur für Kommunikationsnetze, Frau Karin Domel, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .Ergänzende Informationen:Nur schwerbehinderte oder ihnen gleichgestellte PersonenAnforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: ForschungErweiterte Kenntnisse: Mechatronik, Elektrotechnik, Elektronik, Informatik, Entwicklung, Software-Implementierung

The TRR404 “Next Generation Electronics With Active Devices in Three Dimensions [Active-3D]” is a Collaborative Research Center/Transregio between TUD Dresden University of Technology and Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule Aachen (RWTH Aachen) funded by Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft. The TRR aims at exploring a completely new approach for microelectronics technology and therefore teams up materialists, electrical engineers, and computer scientists of TUD, RWTH Aachen and Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mikro- und Optoelektronik mbH (AMO) in Aachen, Forschungszentrum Jülich (FZJ), Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics Halle (MPI-MSP), Nanoelectronic Materials Laboratory gGmbH (NaMLab) in Dresden, Ruhr-Universität Bochum (RUB).For the initial funding phase (April 2025 – December 2028), the TRR404 offers several PhD and Postdoc positions with starting dates from April 1, 2025 onwards. All vacancies can be found here: https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/trr-vacancies (https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/trr-vacancies) .For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At TUD the TRR404 offers, subject to the availability of resources, a full-time position asResearch Associate (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited to 24 months with the option of extension subject to further projects. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The position offers the chance to obtain further academic qualification. Please indicate your request in your application.Position#5:              TRR404-TUD-B06Project:                     B06 System Models, Architectures, and Application Mapping Tools Project Leader:    Prof. Jeronimo Castrillon (Chair of Compiler Construction)Tasks:The PhD student will be mostly in charge of modeling operations of emerging computing architectures, designing compiler abstractions, and working towards a programming framework for the 3D systems.Requirements: - excellent university degree (Master/ diploma or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering or a relevant area- sound knowledge in C/C++ software development, experience in compilers (LLVM, MLIR) and automatic code optimization, knowledgeable in computer architecture- above-average degree achieved in short study period- willingness and ability to think beyond the boundaries of your field, to act in an international and diverse environment and to live an open and constructive communication- strong analytic and problem-solving skills, creativity- an independent, target- and solution-driven work attitude- fluency in English, knowledge of German would be a plusWe offer:A varied and challenging research task, embedded in a friendly, inclusive and supportive team of the TRR’s Principal Investigators (i.e., project leaders and supervisors). We maintain an open and cooperative work attitude with maximum personal responsibility, mutual support with a solution-oriented approach, and flexible working hours where possible. As a PhD student you will be integrated in the TRR’s Graduate School as well as becoming a member of the TUD’ Graduate Academy. Both will offer tailored educational programs and individual supervision agreements.In addition, TUD offers: - employment in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement for the public service of the Länder (TV-L)- an individual assignment of the collective agreement experience level taking into account your previous professional experience- 30 days annual vacation (based on a 5-day workweek) and annual bonus payment (restrictions apply)- additional pension scheme (VBL)- very good accessibility by public transport- car parking facilities- state-of-the-art buildings with labs equipped to a high technical standard- a wide range of offers for health promotion and for the compatibility of family and career- numerous opportunities for further training, including language courses, IT courses and other coursesTUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.Application:Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents including a motivation letter, CV, copy of degree certificate, transcript of grades (i.e., the official list of coursework including your grades) and proof of English language skills, by October 30, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file quoting the reference number TRR404-TUD-B06 in the subject header to jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, Chair of Compiler Construction, Prof. Jerónimo Castrillón, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your DayAs Manager (f/m/d) 9HL PDT, you will lead a global team of highly skilled turbine frame professionals responsible for the SGT-9000HL frame turbine module. You will provide technical and people leadership across product development, design, validation, fleet improvement, and lifecycle support while ensuring effective interfaces with manufacturing, service, procurement, fleet management, product management, and project organizations. You will translate complex technical and business priorities into clear direction, accountable work packages, and timely decisions that strengthen product reliability, performance, cost competitiveness, and customer value.How You’ll Make an Impact * Lead, coach, and develop a global team of engineering professionals, ensuring strong performance, capability growth, and successful execution of turbine development activities.* Define and drive the technical strategy, priorities, and execution roadmap for SGT-9000HL turbine-module development, upgrades, fleet improvements, and issue-resolution initiatives.* Lead complex turbine frame design reviews and technical decision-making across the full product lifecycle, from concept development through manufacturing, testing, verification, validation, and product release.* Direct technical programs, root cause analyses (RCA), and design down-selection activities, ensuring delivery within quality, schedule, and budget targets.* Own resource planning, budget allocation, and manpower management, while establishing robust engineering processes and clear work packages to achieve business objectives.* Foster long-term technology roadmap execution.What You Bring* Master’s degree or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a comparable engineering discipline* Extensive experience in gas turbine product design and development, including turbine frames, hot gas path components, and mechanical integrity* Advanced expertise in gas turbine engineering, heat transfer, turbine module development, and relevant engineering tools such as Siemens NX, Teamcenter, and SAP* Proven leadership and development of diverse, global engineering teams, including coaching, resource planning, and jobs.occupation: Senior Principal Peptide Scientist - External API Development (all genders) (Biochemiker/in)
jobs.description: At Bayer we’re visionaries, driven to solve the world’s toughest challenges and striving for a world where ,Health for all, Hunger for none’ is no longer a dream, but a real possibility. We’re doing it with energy, curiosity and sheer dedication, always learning from unique perspectives of those around us, expanding our thinking, growing our capabilities and redefining ‘impossible’. There are so many reasons to join us. If you’re hungry to build a varied and meaningful career in a community of brilliant and diverse minds to make a real difference, there’s only one choice.Senior Principal Peptide Scientist - External API Development (all genders)As a Senior Principal Peptide Scientist External API Development (m/f/d), you shape the chemical foundation of our peptide pipeline by defining and delivering phase-appropriate drug substance strategies, synthetic routes, manufacturing processes, and supply solutions through an external CDMO network. In this role, you represent Drug Substance Chemistry within the global CMC Technical Development team and are accountable for the drug substance contribution to the overall CMC package. Apply if you want to combine scientific leadership with strategic decision-making and pragmatic execution across development and manufacturing.YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES- You lead the design, evaluation, and optimization of synthetic routes and manufacturing processes for peptide APIs, balancing speed, quality, safety, cost, sustainability, scalability, and process understanding- You define phase-appropriate drug substance strategies and select suitable peptide synthesis, purification, isolation, and manufacturing approaches- You Provide scientific expertise on protecting-group strategies, coupling and deprotection, aggregation, epimerization, oxidation, impurity formation, purification, isolation, and stability- Translating discovery-scale and SAR-driven chemistry into reproducible, scalable, phase-appropriate processes that enable the transition from Discovery into Development is your responsibility- You represent Drug Substance Chemistry in cross-functional CMC project teams and contribute to CMC strategy, risk assessment, development planning, supply planning, and regulatory documentation- You steer, challenge, and approve route design, process development, scale-up, and manufacturing proposals from external partners- Overseeing external development and manufacturing campaigns for toxicology studies, clinical trials, registration, launch, and commercial supply, including timelines, risks, budgets, supply scenarios, and partner deliverables is part of your function- Lead process transfers across external partners and into internal development or manufacturing organizations, ensuring knowledge continuity, documentation, troubleshooting, and compliance falls under your responsibilityWHO YOU ARE- You hold a PhD in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, peptide chemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a closely related scientific discipline- You bring strong expertise in peptide drug substance development and manufacturing, including solid-phase, liquid-phase, hybrid, fragment-based, and emerging synthesis technologies- Your hands-on experience in API process development, scale-up, manufacturing, and scientific troubleshooting within an external CDMO model sets you apart- You demonstrate a solid understanding of phase-appropriate CMC requirements, including strategy development, risk assessment, development and supply planning, and CMC documentation- Building process understanding and contributing to control strategy concepts for impurities, purification, isolation, and stability is what you are confident in- You communicate clearly and manage stakeholders effectively in global, cross-functional project environments while making pragmatic decisions- You apply a strong quality, regulatory, safety, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA BiologyThe Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience.
